metadata.disclaimer: OSA's own analysis of PCI DSS v4.0.1 against SP 800-53 Rev 5. PCI DSS v4.0.1 is by PCI SSC, the PCI Security Standards Council, which owns its text. OSA uses its requirement numbers and says which requirements apply only to service providers. The titles, pairs, rationale and gaps are OSA's own. Each clause is one of the 257 numbered requirements an assessor tests. The coverage figure estimates how much of the requirement the listed controls meet when put in place as written. Read the standard in PCI SSC's document library, and check each requirement against it before you use this mapping for compliance or audit.

metadata.clause_titles_note: OSA's own short titles. The requirement numbers are PCI DSS's, and PCI SSC owns the standard's text, so the titles, rationale and gaps are OSA's own words. clause_group_titles names the 12 principal requirements and Appendices A1 and A2 in OSA's words, by PCI DSS's number: requirement 8.4.3 sits in principal requirement 8, and A1.2.1 in Appendix A1.

clause_fields.section: The PCI DSS section the requirement sits under, by its number: 8.4 for requirement 8.4.3
clause_fields.service_providers_only: true where PCI DSS applies the requirement to service providers only. Every requirement in Appendix A1 carries it, because that appendix applies to multi-tenant service providers. Other requirements leave the key out

edition.replaced: Until 1 November 2026 this mapping had 74 rows, mostly at the level of the sub-requirements, such as 1.2 and 8.3, titled in PCI DSS's own words. It now maps each of the numbered requirements an assessor tests, 257 in all, with titles in OSA's words.

analysis.basis: OSA's own analysis, from PCI DSS's text by three independent ratings. NIST's catalogue of registered crosswalks lists one mapping of PCI DSS v4.0.1, to the Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, posted by an independent developer on 23 December 2025. It has none to SP 800-53 (checked 1 November 2026).

analysis.controls: SP 800-53 Rev 5.2.0 base controls, current ones only. An enhancement that addresses a requirement counts for its base control, and the rationale names it. The multi-factor authentication requirements for the organisation's own users and administrators, 8.4.1, 8.4.2 and 8.5.1, list IA-02, whose enhancements ask for multi-factor authentication. Customer accounts and remote access that includes customers take IA-08. 8.3.10.1, on passwords as the only factor for customer accounts, lists it with IA-05. 8.4.3, multi-factor authentication for remote access from outside, which takes in vendors and customers, lists it with IA-02, and its rationale says that NIST writes IA-02 for the organisation's own users. Each x.1.1 requirement lists the policy and procedures controls, the -01s, of the families its principal requirement draws on. Each x.1.2 adds PS-09 for the duties in position descriptions, and 9.1.2, 10.1.2 and 11.1.2 add AT-03 for training the people who hold them. RA-03 is listed where PCI DSS lets a targeted risk analysis set how often the work is done, such as 5.3.2.1, 8.6.3 and 11.3.1.1, and where it asks for an assessment of risk itself, such as 12.3.1, 12.3.2 and A2.1.2. SP 800-53 writes its supplier controls from the customer's side. So the duties a service provider owes its customers, in 11.4.7, 12.9.1 and 12.9.2, list controls the provider runs, or SA-09 as the customer's side of the duty, and carry lower coverage.
analysis.method: Six AI raters worked in two groups of three. One group rated the 136 requirements of Requirements 1 to 8, and the other the 121 of Requirements 9 to 12 and Appendices A1 and A2. Each rater worked on its own, from each requirement's text, applicability notes, customized approach objective and purpose, and from the control statements. None saw another's rating. OSA lists a control for a requirement where at least two of the three raters in its group named it. The coverage figure is the median of the three estimates of how much of the requirement an organisation would meet by putting the listed controls in place. OSA wrote the titles, rationale and gaps after the controls were settled, from the raters' reasons and the gaps at least two of them named.
analysis.agreement_measure: The Jaccard index of each two ratings: the pairs both named, divided by the pairs either named.

agreement_by_group.requirements_rated: Requirements 9 to 12 and Appendices A1 and A2

analysis.agreement_by_group_note: Each group had its own three ratings, A, B and C. The overall figures pool the ratings with the same letter across the two groups. By group, the index runs from 0.83 to 0.87.
analysis.coverage_agreement: The three coverage estimates for a requirement lie within 10 points of each other for 254 of the 257 requirements. The widest spread is 15 points, for 1.2.5, 6.5.6 and 10.6.2.
analysis.pairs_note: The file lists 569 pairs over 139 controls, the 519 named by all three ratings and the 50 named by two. Every requirement lists at least one control. 177 of the 257 list one or two, and 1.5.1, 6.2.4, 11.1.2 and 12.10.1 list the most, 5 each.
analysis.not_mapped: OSA maps every numbered requirement in force in Requirements 1 to 12 and Appendices A1 and A2, 257 in all. PCI DSS v4.0.1 replaced three requirements on 31 March 2025, and OSA maps their successors: 6.4.1 by 6.4.2, 8.3.10 by 8.3.10.1 and 10.7.1 by 10.7.2. Appendix A3, the designated entities supplemental validation (A3.1.1 to A3.5.1, 20 requirements), applies only to entities that a payment brand or acquirer designates, so OSA leaves it out of this mapping.

clauses.title: Policies and procedures for network security
clauses.rationale: SC-01 and CM-01 ask for documented policies and procedures for communications protection and for configuration management, shared with the people who need them and reviewed on a set cycle. Together they govern how network security controls are set up and changed.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the procedures to be in daily use and known to all who apply them. Check that staff follow them.

clauses.title: Roles and duties for network security
clauses.rationale: SC-01 and CM-01 ask the communications protection and configuration management policies to set out roles and responsibilities. PS-09 writes those security duties into the position descriptions of the people who run network security controls.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the people given these duties to understand them. Confirm that each one does, for example with a briefing or a signed acknowledgement.

clauses.title: Written standards for network security control rulesets
clauses.rationale: CM-02 holds a documented, current baseline for each network security control and keeps it under configuration control. CM-06 sets restrictive settings from common secure configurations, applies them and approves any deviation. SC-07 arranges boundary devices to fit the security architecture, and SC-07(04) sets a traffic flow policy for each managed interface, which is its ruleset.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for standards that govern the rules themselves as well as the device settings. Write ruleset standards for each kind of network security control in use.

clauses.title: Change control for network connections and device settings
clauses.rationale: CM-03 names the types of change under configuration control, then reviews, approves, records and implements each one. CM-04 analyses the security impact of a change before it goes ahead.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Network diagram of every CDE connection, wireless included
clauses.rationale: PL-02 asks the system security plan to describe the operating environment and its connections to other systems, and to stay current as they change. CA-09 authorises internal connections and documents each one's interface, security requirements and the information it carries.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for an accurate network diagram that shows every connection into and out of the CDE, wireless networks included. Draw one and keep it current.

clauses.title: Data-flow diagram of every path account data takes
clauses.rationale: CM-12 records where account data is processed and stored, on which components, and documents any change to those locations. CM-13 maps the system's data actions and the components involved. SP 800-53 writes it for personal data, and the same map can trace account data.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a diagram that traces account data between systems and network segments. Redraw it whenever the environment changes.

clauses.title: Business need for each allowed service, protocol and port
clauses.rationale: CM-07 limits each system to essential capabilities and prohibits or restricts the ports, protocols and services the organisation names. SC-07(04) records each exception to the traffic flow policy with its business need and how long it lasts. SC-07(05) denies all other traffic by default.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the organisation to approve each allowed service, protocol and port and record its business need. Keep the approver and the reason with each entry.

clauses.title: Network safeguards for insecure services and ports in use
clauses.rationale: CM-07 restricts the ports, protocols and services the organisation names as insecure, and CM-07(01) reviews systems for them on a set cycle. CM-06 hardens the settings of whatever stays in use, and it documents and approves each deviation.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the organisation to assess the risk of each insecure service, protocol or port in use and add features that reduce it. Record the protection chosen for each one.

clauses.title: Six-monthly review of network security control settings
clauses.rationale: CM-02 reviews and updates the baseline of each network security control at a frequency the organisation sets. CM-07(01) looks for unneeded or insecure ports, protocols and services on a set cycle and removes them. SC-07(04) reviews the exceptions to each traffic flow policy and drops those that have lost their business need.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for this review at least every six months. Set that interval in CM-02, CM-07(01) and SC-07(04).

clauses.title: Protected configuration files that match live settings
clauses.rationale: AC-03 enforces approved access to stored configuration files, scripts and backups. CM-05 limits who can change network security control settings and the files that hold them. CM-02 keeps a current baseline under configuration control, the reference that stored copies and live settings should both match.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the stored copies of each configuration, backups and scripts included, to match what is live. Compare them with the running settings on a regular schedule and correct any drift.

clauses.title: Deny-by-default filtering of traffic into the CDE
clauses.rationale: AC-04 enforces approved flow control policies, so only authorised traffic enters the CDE. SC-07 monitors and controls traffic at the CDE's managed interfaces. SC-07(05) denies traffic by default and allows it by exception, and SC-07(11) routes incoming traffic only from authorised sources to authorised destinations.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Deny-by-default filtering of traffic leaving the CDE
clauses.rationale: AC-04 enforces approved flow control policies for traffic leaving the CDE. SC-07 controls traffic at the CDE's managed interfaces, and SC-07(05) denies it by default and allows it by exception. SC-07(10) adds measures that prevent the exfiltration of information.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Filtering between every wireless network and the CDE
clauses.rationale: AC-18 sets configuration and connection requirements for each type of wireless access and authorises it before connections start. AC-04 lets only approved wireless flows into the CDE. SC-07 places managed interfaces between wireless segments and the CDE, and SC-07(05) denies traffic by default.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Network security controls at every untrusted boundary
clauses.rationale: SC-07 monitors and controls traffic at external and key internal managed interfaces. It connects to outside networks only through boundary protection devices, and it keeps publicly accessible components in separate subnetworks.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Inbound rules for public services and stateful replies
clauses.rationale: AC-04 enforces approved flows from untrusted to trusted networks. SC-07 keeps publicly accessible components in a separate subnetwork. SC-07(05) denies traffic by default, and SC-07(11) routes incoming traffic only from authorised sources to authorised destinations.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS also lets in replies to sessions that systems inside the trusted network started. Use stateful filtering so that only those replies come back through the boundary.

clauses.title: Blocking spoofed source addresses at the network edge
clauses.rationale: SC-07(11) routes incoming traffic only from authorised sources to authorised destinations. Its guidance uses source address validation to drop illegal addresses and internal-only ones arriving from outside. SI-04 monitors for attacks and their indicators, and SI-04(04) watches inbound traffic against criteria the organisation sets, such as forged source addresses.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the organisation to stop packets with forged source addresses at the edge of the trusted network. Configure ingress filters that drop outside packets claiming internal or reserved addresses.

clauses.title: Cardholder data stores reachable only from trusted networks
clauses.rationale: AC-04 blocks flows from untrusted networks straight to the systems that store cardholder data. SC-07 keeps internal components apart from public subnetworks. SC-07(21) isolates chosen components behind boundary protection, and SC-07(28) prohibits their direct connection to a public network.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS covers every component that stores cardholder data, cloud databases included. Place each one behind the internal boundary, reachable only from trusted networks.

clauses.title: Keeping internal addresses and routing details private
clauses.rationale: SC-07 guards the managed interfaces at the boundary. SC-07(16) prevents discovery of the components that form a managed interface, for example by address translation or by leaving their addresses out of DNS. SC-07(04) blocks unauthorised exchange of control plane traffic, such as routing, with outside networks.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS limits internal addressing and routing details to authorised parties. Keep them out of public DNS and error messages, and share network documents only with approved recipients.

clauses.title: Locked-down devices that reach the CDE and untrusted networks
clauses.rationale: AC-19 sets configuration and connection requirements for organisation-controlled mobile devices and authorises each connection. AC-20 sets terms and required controls for personally owned and other external devices. CM-06 defines the mandatory security settings and approves each deviation. AC-06(10) keeps non-privileged users from disabling or altering security controls. SC-07(12) adds host-based protection such as personal firewalls, and SC-07(07) prevents split tunnelling.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS lets users alter these controls only with documented management approval, case by case and for a set period. Keep the controls running at all other times.

clauses.title: Policies and procedures for secure configuration
clauses.rationale: CM-01 asks for a documented configuration management policy and procedures, shared with the people who need them and reviewed and updated on a set cycle. They govern how every system component is configured securely.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the procedures to be in daily use and known to all who apply them. Check that staff follow them.

clauses.title: Roles and duties for secure configuration
clauses.rationale: CM-01 asks the configuration management policy to set out roles and responsibilities. PS-09 writes those security duties into the position descriptions of the people who configure system components.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the people given these duties to understand them. Confirm that each one does, for example with a briefing or a signed acknowledgement.

clauses.title: Hardening standards for every system component
clauses.rationale: CM-06 takes settings from common secure configurations, such as hardening guides, applies them to each component and approves any deviation. CM-06(01) can manage and verify those settings by automated means. CM-02 keeps a current baseline for each system and updates it on a set cycle and when components are installed or upgraded.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the organisation to update the standards as new vulnerabilities come to light. Check each new system against them when it goes into production.

clauses.title: Removing or securing vendor default accounts
clauses.rationale: AC-02 defines the account types allowed and disables or removes unneeded accounts. IA-05 changes default authenticators, such as vendor passwords, before first use.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Separating functions with different security needs
clauses.rationale: CM-07 limits each component to essential capabilities, and its guidance favours one function per component where feasible. SC-32 places components in separate physical or logical domains on grounds the organisation sets. SC-39 gives each process its own execution domain, for example through virtualisation or sandboxing.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for functions that share a component without isolation to meet the strictest need among them. Harden the whole component to that level.

clauses.title: Stripping unneeded services and functions from systems
clauses.rationale: CM-07 configures each system to provide only essential capabilities and prohibits or restricts the functions, ports, protocols and services the organisation names. CM-07(01) reviews systems on a set cycle and disables or removes what is unnecessary or insecure.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Justifying and protecting insecure services on systems
clauses.rationale: CM-07 limits each insecure protocol, service or daemon the organisation names to approved cases. CM-06 documents and approves each deviation from the secure settings, with its operational reason.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for added security features on each insecure service, protocol or daemon that stays in use. Record the features for each one and confirm they are in place.

clauses.title: Security parameters set as tightly as operations allow
clauses.rationale: CM-06 sets each component's security parameters to the most restrictive mode that operations allow, using common secure configurations. It implements those settings, approves any deviation and controls later changes.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Encrypting every administrative session over the network
clauses.rationale: AC-17 sets the requirements for each type of remote access, and AC-17(02) protects remote sessions with cryptographic mechanisms. SC-08 protects transmitted information, and SC-08(01) uses cryptography to prevent its disclosure and detect changes in transit. SC-13 names each use of cryptography and the type it requires, which lets the organisation set strong cryptography for administrative access.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Replacing factory defaults on wireless equipment
clauses.rationale: AC-18 sets configuration requirements for each type of wireless access and authorises it before use. IA-05 changes default authenticators, such as access point passwords and preset keys, before first use. CM-06 applies secure settings in place of other insecure vendor defaults, SNMP community strings included.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Changing wireless keys after departures or a compromise
clauses.rationale: IA-05 changes authenticators when events the organisation names occur, and changes shared ones when a group's membership changes. It also sets procedures for compromised authenticators. SC-12 manages cryptographic keys to the organisation's rules for their generation, distribution, storage, access and destruction.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a new wireless key when anyone who knows it leaves or changes role, and when a compromise is known or suspected. Write those events into IA-05 and the SC-12 key rules as triggers.

clauses.title: Policies and procedures for stored account data
clauses.rationale: SC-01, MP-01 and SI-01 each ask for a documented policy and procedures, shared with the people who need them and reviewed on a set cycle. SC-01 governs encryption and key management. MP-01 governs the media that hold account data, and SI-01 the retention and disposal of data.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the procedures to be in daily use and known to all who apply them. Check that the staff who handle stored account data follow them.

clauses.title: Roles and duties for stored account data
clauses.rationale: SC-01, MP-01 and SI-01 each ask for a policy that sets out roles and responsibilities. SC-01 covers encryption and key management. MP-01 covers media handling, and SI-01 retention and disposal. PS-09 writes these security duties into position descriptions.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the people given these duties to understand them. Confirm that each one does, for example with a briefing or a signed acknowledgement.

clauses.title: Retention limits and secure deletion of account data
clauses.rationale: CM-12 records each place where account data is stored and processed. SI-12 manages and retains information as the law and operational needs require. SI-12(01) limits the personal data held to the elements the organisation names, and SI-12(03) disposes of data when its retention period ends. MP-06 sanitises media before disposal or reuse, and MP-06(01) verifies each sanitisation.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a check every three months that data held past its retention period is gone. Schedule that check, and cover any SAD stored before authorisation in the retention policy.

clauses.title: Erasing all SAD after authorisation, encrypted or not
clauses.rationale: SI-12 manages how long information is kept, so the organisation can end the retention of SAD at authorisation. SI-12(01) limits the personal data held to a set list of elements. SI-12(03) erases data by the organisation's chosen techniques once its retention period ends.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for all SAD to be made unrecoverable at authorisation, encrypted copies included. Search databases, logs and files for stray copies and purge them.

clauses.title: Discarding full track data after authorisation
clauses.rationale: SI-12 manages how long information is kept. SI-12(01) limits the personal data held to the elements the organisation names. The organisation can name the PAN, cardholder name, expiry date and service code, and leave full track data out.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for full track data to be erased once authorisation completes. Search databases, logs and debug output for any that remains and remove it.

clauses.title: Discarding the card verification code after authorisation
clauses.rationale: SI-12 manages and retains information as the law and operational needs require. The organisation uses it to end the retention of the card verification code when authorisation completes.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the card verification code to be erased at authorisation. Search databases, logs and call recordings for the code and purge any copy found.

clauses.title: Discarding the PIN and PIN block after authorisation
clauses.rationale: SI-12 manages and retains information as the law and operational needs require. The organisation uses it to end the retention of PINs and PIN blocks when authorisation completes.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for PINs and PIN blocks to be erased once authorisation completes. Search systems, logs and files for any copies and remove them.

clauses.title: Strong encryption for SAD stored before authorisation
clauses.rationale: SC-28 protects information at rest, and SC-28(01) encrypts it on the components and media the organisation names. Here that means every electronic store of SAD held before authorisation. SC-13 sets the type of cryptography each use requires.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: SAD held by issuers, limited to need and encrypted
clauses.rationale: SI-12 retains information as operational needs require, here the needs of the issuing function. AC-03 enforces approved access to the stored SAD. SC-28 protects it at rest, and SC-28(01) encrypts it. SC-13 sets the type of cryptography each use requires.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks issuers and the companies that support them to keep only the SAD their issuing work needs. Record that need for each SAD element they store.

clauses.title: Masking the PAN wherever it is shown
clauses.rationale: AC-03 enforces approved access rules, and AC-03(07) bases them on roles, so only the roles allowed to see the full PAN can do so. AC-06 grants each person only the access their duties need.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS sets the most a display may show at the BIN and the last four digits. Build that masking into every screen and printout, and show more only to people with a business need for it.

clauses.title: Stopping PAN being copied or moved in remote sessions
clauses.rationale: AC-17 sets usage restrictions and connection rules for each type of remote access. AC-04 enforces approved information flows, so PAN stays inside the remote session. AC-06 gives the right to copy or move PAN only to people whose duties need it.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for copying and moving PAN over remote access to be blocked for all but approved people. Turn off clipboard, file transfer, drive mapping and printing by default, and record who is approved and why.

clauses.title: Hashing, truncating, tokenising or encrypting stored PAN
clauses.rationale: SC-28 protects information at rest, and SC-28(01) encrypts it on the components and media the organisation names, which can include backups and logs. SC-13 sets the cryptography for each use, such as hashing or encryption. SC-12 manages the keys. SI-19 removes named elements of personal data from datasets, and SI-19(04) masks, hashes or replaces direct identifiers, as truncation and tokens do.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for controls that stop hashed and truncated versions of one PAN being matched to rebuild it. Keep the versions apart so nobody can combine them.

clauses.title: Keyed hashes of the whole PAN, with managed keys
clauses.rationale: SC-13 sets the cryptography for each use, here a keyed hash, such as an HMAC, over the full PAN. SC-12 manages the secret key behind the hash. SC-28 protects the stored hashes at rest.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for every PAN hash to use a secret key and to cover the whole number. Replace any unkeyed hashes with keyed ones.

clauses.title: Disk encryption as sole PAN protection, removable media only
clauses.rationale: SC-28 protects information at rest, and SC-28(01) encrypts it on the components and media the organisation names. The organisation can limit disk encryption to removable media and apply file, column or field encryption to PAN on fixed storage. SC-13 sets the type of cryptography each use requires.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS accepts disk or partition encryption on its own only for removable media. On fixed storage, also protect PAN at the data level, for example with truncation or column encryption.

clauses.title: Independent login and key handling for disk encryption
clauses.rationale: AC-03 enforces approved access to the decrypted data, which the organisation can make independent of the operating system login. IA-05 and IA-05(06) protect the passwords and keys that unlock the data. SC-12 sets key requirements that can keep decryption keys apart from user accounts. SC-28 protects data at rest, and SC-28(03) gives the keys protected storage.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for disk decryption to need its own login, managed apart from the operating system's accounts. Set up that separate unlock step for every encrypted disk.

clauses.title: Protecting data keys and the keys that wrap them
clauses.rationale: SC-12 sets the organisation's rules for key storage and access, key-encrypting keys included. AC-06 limits key access to the custodians whose duties need it. SC-28 protects information at rest, and SC-28(03) gives keys protected storage.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for each key-encrypting key to be equal to or stronger than the keys it protects, and stored apart from them. Write both rules into the key procedures.

clauses.title: Service provider's record of its cryptographic design
clauses.rationale: PL-08 asks for a security architecture, which here sets out how cryptography protects stored account data. SC-13 names each use of cryptography and the type it needs. SC-12 sets key requirements that can record each key's purpose, strength and expiry. CM-08 inventories system components, HSMs and key management systems among them, with details the organisation chooses, such as type and location.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the service provider to keep production keys out of test environments. State that rule in the architecture description.

clauses.title: Approved storage forms for secret and private keys
clauses.rationale: SC-12 sets the organisation's key storage requirements, which can name the forms allowed, such as wrapped keys, keys held in hardware or key shares. SC-12(02) produces, controls and distributes symmetric keys with FIPS-validated or NSA-approved technology. SC-28 protects information at rest, and SC-28(03) keeps keys in protected storage, such as a hardware-protected key store.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for key shares from an approved random number generator in a secure cryptographic device, or under ISO 19592 or an equal standard. Generate every share one of those ways.

clauses.title: Fewest custodians for cleartext key components
clauses.rationale: AC-06 gives access to cleartext key components only to the custodians whose duties need it, which keeps their number small. SC-12 sets the key access rules that say who may handle key components.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Keeping keys in as few places as possible
clauses.rationale: SC-12 manages keys under storage requirements the organisation sets. Those requirements can name the places where keys may be held and limit them to the fewest the business needs.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for keys to sit in the fewest places possible. List every place a key is held, and keep only the copies the business needs.

clauses.title: Generating strong keys for stored account data
clauses.rationale: SC-12 sets the organisation's requirements for key generation. SC-12(02) and (03) name the technology and processes for producing symmetric and asymmetric keys. SC-13 sets the type of cryptography for each use, and with it the algorithm and key strength.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Delivering keys securely to their custodians
clauses.rationale: SC-12 sets the organisation's key distribution requirements, which can send keys only to authorised custodians by secure means. SC-12(02) and (03) name the technology and processes for distributing symmetric and asymmetric keys.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Storing keys securely as part of key management
clauses.rationale: SC-12 sets the organisation's key storage requirements. SC-28 protects information at rest, and SC-28(03) gives cryptographic keys protected storage, through safeguards the organisation names or a hardware-protected key store.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Changing each key when its cryptoperiod ends
clauses.rationale: SC-12 manages keys across their life under requirements the organisation sets. Those requirements can give each key type a lifetime and a process for replacing keys when it ends.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the organisation to set a cryptoperiod for every key type and to change each key when its period ends. Record both in the SC-12 key requirements.

clauses.title: Retiring or replacing weakened and compromised keys
clauses.rationale: SC-12 manages keys through their life, destruction included, under requirements the organisation sets, such as when to retire or replace a key. PS-04 revokes the authenticators and credentials of anyone who leaves. Here that reaches the key components a departing custodian knew.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a key change on suspected compromise and when a custodian who knew a key component leaves or changes role. Take retired keys out of encryption use.

clauses.title: Dual control and split knowledge in manual key handling
clauses.rationale: AC-03 enforces approved access, and AC-03(02) requires two people to authorise the actions the organisation names, such as manual key operations. AC-05 separates duties so one person never holds a whole key. SC-12 sets how manual key operations run and can require key components held by different people.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for key components from an approved random number generator in a secure cryptographic device, or under ISO 19592 or an equal standard. Generate each custodian's component one of those ways.

clauses.title: Guarding keys against unauthorised substitution
clauses.rationale: AC-03 enforces approved access, so only authorised people can load or replace keys. SC-12 sets the organisation's key management requirements, which can require authorisation before any key is replaced.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for safeguards that stop anyone swapping in a key of their own. Verify each key before it is loaded, for example with a key check value.

clauses.title: Key custodians' signed acceptance of their duties
clauses.rationale: PL-04 gives custodians written rules for their duties and takes their documented acknowledgement before granting access, renewed when the rules change. PS-06 has them sign an access agreement before receiving key access, and sign again when it changes.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Service provider's key guidance for customers
clauses.rationale: SA-05 produces user documentation on secure use and user duties, and distributes it to the people the organisation names, here customers that receive shared keys. SC-12 sets key management requirements that cover keys shared with customers, including how they are distributed and stored.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the service provider to give every customer that receives shared keys written guidance on sending, storing and updating them. Add that guidance to the customer documentation.

clauses.title: Policies and procedures for encryption in transit
clauses.rationale: SC-01 asks for a documented policy and procedures for communications protection, shared with the people who need them and reviewed on a set cycle. They govern how the organisation protects cardholder data sent across public networks.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the procedures to be in daily use and known to all who apply them. Check that staff follow the procedures for encryption in transit.

clauses.title: Roles and duties for encryption in transit
clauses.rationale: SC-01 asks for a communications protection policy that sets out roles and responsibilities, including those for protecting data in transit. PS-09 writes those security duties into the position descriptions of the people who carry them out.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the people given these duties to understand them. Confirm that each one does, for example with a briefing or a signed acknowledgement.

clauses.title: Strong cryptography for PAN sent over public networks
clauses.rationale: SC-08(01) encrypts PAN while it crosses public networks. SC-13 has the organisation set the cryptography each use requires. SC-17 issues certificates under a set policy or obtains them from an approved provider, and keeps only approved trust anchors in trust stores. IA-05(02) validates each certificate's path to an accepted trust anchor and checks its revocation status.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks each connection to refuse fallback to insecure protocol versions and to reject expired certificates. Build both into the settings for SC-13 and IA-05(02).

clauses.title: Inventory of keys and certificates for PAN in transit
clauses.rationale: SC-12 manages the cryptographic keys that protect PAN in transit, from generation to destruction, under rules the organisation sets. SC-17 governs the certificates the organisation issues or obtains and the trust anchors its trust stores hold.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for an up-to-date inventory of every key and certificate that protects PAN in transit. Record each one's strength, owner and expiry date.

clauses.title: Wireless encryption and authentication for PAN and the CDE
clauses.rationale: AC-18 sets configuration and connection rules for each type of wireless access and authorises it before connections start. AC-18(01) protects wireless access with authentication of users or devices and with encryption. SC-08(01) encrypts the data sent over wireless links. SC-13 has the organisation choose the cryptography each use requires.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Encrypting PAN sent by email and other messaging tools
clauses.rationale: SC-08(01) uses cryptography to prevent unauthorised disclosure of information in transit, which covers PAN sent by email, chat or other messaging tools. SC-13 has the organisation choose the cryptography for that use.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for PAN to travel only on messaging channels that encrypt it. Block it on every other channel, and delete any PAN that arrives through one.

clauses.title: Policies and procedures for malware protection
clauses.rationale: SI-01 asks for a documented policy and procedures for system and information integrity, shared with those who need them and reviewed on a set cycle. They govern how the organisation guards its systems against malware.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the procedures to be in daily use and known to all who apply them. Check that staff follow the anti-malware procedures.

clauses.title: Roles and duties for malware protection
clauses.rationale: SI-01 asks for an integrity policy that sets out roles and responsibilities, including those for malware protection. PS-09 writes those security duties into the position descriptions of the people who carry them out.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the people given these duties to understand them. Confirm that each one does, for example with a briefing or a signed acknowledgement.

clauses.title: Anti-malware on every system component
clauses.rationale: SI-03 places malicious code protection at system entry and exit points, such as mail gateways and endpoints, to detect and remove malicious code.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for anti-malware on every system component. Exempt a component only when a recorded evaluation under 5.2.3 finds it free of malware risk.

clauses.title: Detecting and stopping every known kind of malware
clauses.rationale: SI-03 detects and removes malicious code, using signature or non-signature methods. On each detection it blocks or quarantines the code and alerts the people the organisation names.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Reviewing components exempted from anti-malware
clauses.rationale: RA-03 identifies threats to the components exempted from anti-malware and updates that assessment on a cycle the organisation sets. SI-05 receives security alerts and advisories from outside sources, such as news of new malware, and passes them to the people who act on them.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a written list of the components exempted from anti-malware. At each review, record whether each one stays exempt.

clauses.title: Risk-based interval for reviewing exempted components
clauses.rationale: RA-03 asks for a documented risk assessment, reviewed and updated on a cycle the organisation sets. That assessment gives the organisation a basis for how often it re-evaluates the components exempted from anti-malware.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the interval to come from a targeted risk analysis that meets 12.3.1. Document that analysis and the interval it sets.

clauses.title: Automatic updates to anti-malware tools
clauses.rationale: SI-03 updates the malicious code protection mechanisms automatically whenever new releases are available. The organisation's configuration management policy and procedures govern how those updates roll out.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Malware scans or continuous behaviour analysis
clauses.rationale: SI-03 runs periodic scans at a frequency the organisation sets, and real-time scans of files from outside sources as they are downloaded or opened. Its non-signature methods detect malicious code by how it behaves.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Risk-based interval for periodic malware scans
clauses.rationale: SI-03 runs periodic malware scans at a frequency the organisation sets. RA-03 gives the organisation a documented, regularly updated risk assessment to base that frequency on.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the scan frequency to come from a targeted risk analysis that meets 12.3.1. Document that analysis and set the SI-03 frequency from it.

clauses.title: Scanning removable media on connection
clauses.rationale: SI-03 scans files from external sources in real time at the endpoint as they are opened or run. That covers files on removable media, such as USB drives.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for removable media to be scanned automatically, or its use watched by behavioural analysis, as soon as it is inserted or mounted. Set the endpoint protection to act on connection.

clauses.title: Audit logs of anti-malware activity
clauses.rationale: AU-02 has the organisation name anti-malware events among the event types it logs, and AU-12 has the components generate audit records for them. AU-11 keeps those records for a period the organisation sets.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks, through 10.5.1, for at least 12 months of log history, with the latest three months on hand for analysis. Set that period in AU-11.

clauses.title: Stopping users from disabling or changing anti-malware
clauses.rationale: AC-06 limits users to the access their duties need, and AC-06(10) stops non-privileged users from running privileged functions, such as disabling or altering malware protection. CM-05 restricts who may change the system, anti-malware settings included. CM-06 has the organisation document and approve any departure from its configuration settings, such as a temporary pause in protection.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a time limit on every approved pause, with management signing off each one. Record the end date alongside the CM-06 approval.

clauses.title: Detecting and blocking phishing aimed at staff
clauses.rationale: SI-08 puts spam protection at entry points such as mail gateways, where it detects and acts on unsolicited messages. SI-03 scans the attachments and downloads that phishing delivers and blocks or quarantines malicious code.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for defences built for phishing. Verify the senders of incoming mail with authentication such as DMARC, and check links against known phishing sites.

clauses.title: Policies and procedures for secure development and change
clauses.rationale: SA-01, SI-01 and CM-01 ask for documented policies and procedures, shared with the people who need them and reviewed on a set cycle. SA-01 covers how systems and software are acquired and developed. SI-01 covers patching and flaw remediation, and CM-01 covers change control.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the procedures to be in daily use and known to all who apply them. Check that staff follow them.

clauses.title: Roles and duties for secure development and change
clauses.rationale: SA-01, SI-01 and CM-01 ask for policies that set out roles and responsibilities for development, patching and change control. Each names an official to manage its policy. PS-09 writes these security duties into position descriptions.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the people given these duties to understand them. Confirm that each one does, for example with a briefing or a signed acknowledgement.

clauses.title: Secure development life cycle for bespoke and custom code
clauses.rationale: SA-03 runs development under a life cycle that builds in security and ties risk management into each of its activities. SA-08 applies security engineering principles from specification through design, build and change. SA-15 has developers follow a documented process that addresses security requirements and names its standards and tools.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the software to meet the standard's own requirements, such as strong authentication and logging. Write those into each project's security requirements.

clauses.title: Yearly software security training for developers
clauses.rationale: AT-03 gives developers security training for their role before they start work and then at a frequency the organisation sets. It also updates the training content on a set cycle and after set events.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for this training at least every 12 months. Set that frequency in AT-03, and cover secure design and coding in each developer's languages and any testing tools they use.

clauses.title: Security review of code before each release
clauses.rationale: SA-11 has developers test and evaluate their code and correct the flaws found. SA-11(01) adds static code analysis and SA-11(04) adds manual code review. SA-15 names the standards developers follow, which the reviews check the code against.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks each review to look for new kinds of flaw as well as known ones. Keep the review checks current and hold each release until its findings are fixed.

clauses.title: Independent manual code review and management sign-off
clauses.rationale: AC-05 documents duties that need separating, such as writing and reviewing code, and sets access to keep them apart. SA-11(04) asks for manual code review by set processes. CM-03 has each change reviewed and approved before release.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for reviewers who are skilled in code review and in secure coding. Choose reviewers with those skills.

clauses.title: Coding techniques that defend against common attacks
clauses.rationale: SA-08 applies security engineering principles in design and build. SA-15 names the standards and tools developers use. SA-11(01) and (08) run static and dynamic code analysis to find common flaws, and SA-11(02) adds threat modelling. SI-10 checks inputs, and SI-10(06) prevents injection of untrusted data. SI-16 protects memory from unauthorised code execution.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS lists the attack types the techniques must address. Among them are business logic abuse such as XSS and CSRF, misuse of cryptography and bypass of access control. Name a defence for each in the coding standards and tests.

clauses.title: Tracking new vulnerabilities and ranking their risk
clauses.rationale: SI-05 receives security alerts and advisories from outside bodies, such as CERTs, on an ongoing basis. RA-05 monitors for newly reported vulnerabilities and uses standard measures of their impact. SI-02 identifies and reports system flaws, in bespoke and third-party software alike.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for each new vulnerability to get a risk ranking. Define a ranking scheme that marks out every high and critical vulnerability.

clauses.title: Bespoke and custom code inventory with third-party components
clauses.rationale: CM-08 keeps an accurate inventory of all system components, software included, at the level of detail needed for tracking. SR-04 documents and maintains where components come from. SR-04(04) checks the internal make-up and origin of critical components.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the inventory to list the third-party components inside bespoke and custom software. List each library with its version, and use the list to track patches.

clauses.title: Timely security patches, critical ones within a month
clauses.rationale: SI-02 installs security-relevant updates within a time the organisation sets, counted from their release. RA-05 remediates vulnerabilities within response times the organisation sets from its assessment of risk.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS sets a limit of one month from release for critical patches. Set that period in SI-02 and in the response times of RA-05.

clauses.title: Automated defence against attacks on public web applications
clauses.rationale: SC-07 places boundary protection at the external interfaces, where it monitors and controls traffic to public web applications. SI-04 monitors for attacks, SI-04(05) alerts staff to signs of compromise, and SI-04(07) acts to end suspicious events. AU-12 has the protection generate audit records.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the protection to keep running and stay up to date. Set it to block attacks, or to raise alerts that staff investigate at once.

clauses.title: Approving payment page scripts and checking their integrity
clauses.rationale: SC-18 defines acceptable mobile code, such as JavaScript, and authorises and controls its use. SI-07 checks scripts for unauthorised changes, and SI-07(06) does so with cryptographic means such as hashes. CM-08 keeps an inventory of system components, which here lists each script.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a written reason, business or technical, why each script is needed. Record one for every script in the inventory, those from third parties included.

clauses.title: Change control for production systems
clauses.rationale: CM-03 reviews and approves each change with its security impact in view, and records the decision. CM-03(02) tests and documents changes before they are finalised. CM-04 analyses each change for security impact before it is made. SA-11 has developers test bespoke code changes and fix the flaws found. CM-02(03) keeps earlier baseline configurations so a failed change can be rolled back.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Rechecking PCI DSS requirements after a significant change
clauses.rationale: CM-04 analyses the security impact of each change, and CM-04(02) checks afterwards that the affected controls work as intended. PL-02 updates the security plan to reflect changes to the system and its environment.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a check of every applicable requirement on new or changed systems, beyond the controls the change touched. Define what counts as a significant change, and run that check after each one.

clauses.title: Separation of pre-production from production
clauses.rationale: SC-32 places pre-production and production in separate physical or logical domains. AC-03 enforces approved access rules between them. CM-04(01) analyses changes in a separate test environment before they go into production.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Separate duties so only approved changes reach production
clauses.rationale: AC-05 documents duties that need separating, such as pre-production and production work, and sets access to keep them apart. CM-03 puts in place only changes that have been reviewed and approved. CM-05 sets and enforces access restrictions for making changes, and CM-05(05) limits and reviews the privileges to change production.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Keeping live PANs out of pre-production
clauses.rationale: SA-03(02) approves and controls any use of live data in pre-production, and protects that environment to the level of the data in it. PM-25 keeps the personal data used for testing to a minimum and authorises its use where testing needs it.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Removing test data and accounts before go-live
clauses.rationale: AC-02 defines which types of account a system allows and which it prohibits. It removes accounts in line with policy, so test accounts can come off a system before it goes live.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for all test data and test accounts to be cleared before a system goes live. Add a release step that removes both and confirms they are gone.

clauses.title: Policies and procedures for access rights
clauses.rationale: AC-01 asks for a documented access control policy and procedures, shared with the people who need them and reviewed on a set cycle. They govern how the organisation grants and limits access.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the procedures to be in daily use and known to all who apply them. Check that staff follow them.

clauses.title: Roles and duties for access rights
clauses.rationale: AC-01 asks for an access control policy that sets out roles and responsibilities, with a named official to manage it. PS-09 writes these security duties into position descriptions.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the people given these duties to understand them. Confirm that each one does, for example with a briefing or a signed acknowledgement.

clauses.title: Access control model tied to job functions
clauses.rationale: AC-02 defines account types, sets the criteria for group and role membership and records each account's privileges. AC-03 enforces approved access, and AC-03(07) bases it on roles the organisation defines, such as job functions. AC-06 allows each user only the access their tasks need.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Least privilege for every user, administrators included
clauses.rationale: AC-02 grants access on a valid authorisation and the intended use, and assigns each account its roles and privileges. AC-02(07) manages privileged accounts under a role-based or attribute-based scheme. AC-06 allows only the privileges each task needs, and AC-06(05) restricts privileged accounts to named people or roles.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Approval of each privilege by an authorised person
clauses.rationale: AC-02 requires approval from named people or roles before an account is created. It grants access to a system on a valid authorisation for the intended use.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Six-monthly review of user accounts and their privileges
clauses.rationale: AC-02 reviews accounts against the account management rules at a frequency the organisation sets. AC-06(07) reviews the privileges held by each class of user and removes or reassigns them to match business needs.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS sets the review interval at six months at most, with vendor and other third-party accounts included. Set that frequency in AC-02 and AC-06(07), and have management sign off each review.

clauses.title: Least privilege for system and application accounts
clauses.rationale: AC-02 manages system and service accounts like any other account type, and AC-02(11) enforces the conditions under which system accounts may be used. AC-06 gives processes acting for users only the access their tasks need.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Risk-based review of system and application account access
clauses.rationale: AC-02 reviews application and system accounts at a frequency the organisation sets. AC-06(07) reviews the privileges they hold and removes or reassigns any excess. RA-03 assesses risk to the system, which gives a basis for setting how often the reviews happen.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks management to confirm at each review that the access is still right. Record that sign-off with each review.

clauses.title: Limits on querying stored cardholder data
clauses.rationale: AC-03(11) restricts access to data repositories that hold chosen types of information, such as cardholder data. AC-03(07) ties that access to roles. AC-06 limits users to the access their tasks need, and AC-06(05) restricts privileged database accounts to the responsible administrators.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for users to query stored cardholder data through applications that apply role-based limits. Route every user query that way.

clauses.title: Need-to-know access control on every system component
clauses.rationale: AC-03 enforces approved authorisations for logical access to information and system resources. AC-06 allows each user only the access their assigned tasks need, so access follows need to know.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Role-based permissions enforced by the access control system
clauses.rationale: AC-02 sets the criteria for group and role membership and specifies each account's privileges. AC-03 enforces approved authorisations, and AC-03(07) does so through roles the organisation defines, such as job functions.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Default deny in every access control system
clauses.rationale: AC-03 enforces approved authorisations, so each access needs an approval behind it and anything unapproved is refused. AC-06 allows only the authorised accesses that each user's tasks require.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for every access control system to deny access by default. Set each system that way and grant access through specific rules.

clauses.title: Policies and procedures for identification and authentication
clauses.rationale: AC-01 and IA-01 ask for documented policies and procedures for access control and for identification and authentication. Each is shared with the people who need it and reviewed on a set cycle. Together they govern how accounts are managed and how users prove who they are.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the procedures to be in daily use and known to all who apply them. Check that the staff who manage accounts and credentials follow them.

clauses.title: Roles and duties for identification and authentication
clauses.rationale: AC-01 and IA-01 ask for policies that set out roles and responsibilities for access control and for identification and authentication. PS-09 writes those security duties into the position descriptions of the people who hold them.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the people given these duties to understand them. Confirm that each one does, for example with a briefing or a signed acknowledgement.

clauses.title: A unique ID for each user before any access
clauses.rationale: IA-02 uniquely identifies and authenticates each of the organisation's users and ties that identity to the processes acting for them. Every action then traces to one person. IA-04 assigns each identifier to its intended individual once someone with authority approves it, and stops its reuse for a set period.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Shared, group and generic IDs as approved exceptions
clauses.rationale: AC-02 defines which types of account are allowed, and AC-02(09) permits shared and group accounts only under conditions the organisation sets. AC-02(11) enforces usage conditions such as time limits, and AC-02(02) removes or disables temporary and emergency accounts after a set period. IA-02(05) authenticates each person before they reach a shared account, so actions trace to one person.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a business reason and a time limit for each use of a shared ID. Record the reason every time, and enforce the limit through AC-02(11).

clauses.title: Service provider credentials unique to each customer site
clauses.rationale: IA-05 manages authenticators from issue to revocation. IA-05(08) asks for controls the organisation chooses against the risk of one person holding accounts on many systems. A separate authenticator for each customer site is one such control.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the service provider to keep a separate set of credentials for each customer's premises. Make that the control chosen under IA-05(08).

clauses.title: Approval for every change to user IDs and credentials
clauses.rationale: AC-02 requires approval for each new account, specifies the privileges of every account, and creates, changes and removes accounts by the organisation's procedures. IA-04 requires authorisation before anyone assigns an identifier. IA-05 sets procedures for issuing authenticators, replacing lost or compromised ones and revoking them.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Revoking access at once when someone leaves
clauses.rationale: AC-02 notifies account managers within a set time when users are terminated, and aligns account management with termination processes. PS-04 disables system access within a set time when employment ends and revokes the person's authenticators and credentials.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for access to end immediately when someone leaves. Make the time periods in PS-04 and AC-02 immediate.

clauses.title: Disabling user accounts left unused for 90 days
clauses.rationale: AC-02 monitors the use of accounts and disables or removes them under the organisation's rules. AC-02(03) disables an account within a set time once it has been inactive for a period the organisation chooses.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS sets 90 days of inactivity as the limit. Set the two periods in AC-02(03) so an idle account is disabled by day 90.

clauses.title: Time-limited, monitored remote accounts for third parties
clauses.rationale: AC-02 enables and disables accounts under the organisation's rules and monitors their use. AC-02(11) enforces usage conditions on chosen accounts, and AC-02(12) watches for atypical use and reports it. AC-17 authorises each type of remote access, and AC-17(01) monitors and controls it automatically. AC-17(09) can disconnect or disable remote access within a set time. MA-04 approves and monitors remote maintenance and ends the session when the work is done.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for third-party remote accounts to stay disabled between uses. Enable each one for a support task and disable it when the task ends.

clauses.title: Session lock after 15 minutes of idle time
clauses.rationale: AC-11 locks the device after a set period of inactivity and keeps it locked until the user signs in again. AC-12 ends a session automatically under conditions the organisation sets, such as idle time. IA-11 asks users to authenticate again in situations the organisation names.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS sets the idle limit at 15 minutes. Use that value for the AC-11 lock and for the AC-12 and IA-11 triggers.

clauses.title: An authentication factor for every user and administrator
clauses.rationale: IA-02 uniquely identifies and authenticates every user and administrator in the organisation. IA-05 manages the authenticators themselves, such as passwords, tokens and biometrics, and gives each enough strength for its intended use.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Encrypting authentication factors in transit and at rest
clauses.rationale: IA-05 protects authenticator content from disclosure, and IA-05(01) sends passwords only over encrypted channels and stores them with a salted key derivation function. SC-08 protects credentials in transit. SC-28 protects them at rest, and SC-28(01) does so with cryptographic mechanisms. SC-13 has the organisation choose the cryptography for each use.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Confirming identity before any credential reset or change
clauses.rationale: IA-05 verifies the identity of whoever receives an authenticator when it is first issued. It also sets procedures for authenticators that are lost, compromised or damaged, which govern how they are replaced.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the user's identity to be confirmed before every reset or change of a factor, help desk requests included. Extend the IA-05 identity check from first issue to every change.

clauses.title: Account lockout after 10 failed logon attempts
clauses.rationale: AC-07 limits the number of consecutive failed logons a user may make in a set period. Once the limit is passed, it locks the account for a set time or until an administrator releases it.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS caps attempts at 10 and sets a lockout of at least 30 minutes, or until the organisation verifies the user. Set both values in AC-07.

clauses.title: Unique initial and reset passwords, changed at first use
clauses.rationale: IA-05 has the organisation set the initial content of every authenticator it issues. IA-05(01) requires a new password straight after account recovery, such as a reset.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for each first-time or reset password to be unique to its user, and for the user to replace it at first logon. Set both rules in IA-05.

clauses.title: Password length and mix of letters and digits
clauses.rationale: IA-05 gives each authenticator enough strength for its intended use. IA-05(01) enforces the composition and complexity rules the organisation sets for passwords, and lets users choose long passwords and passphrases.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS sets a minimum of 12 characters, mixing letters and digits, with 8 allowed where a system's limit is lower. Set these rules in IA-05(01).

clauses.title: Password history against reuse of recent passwords
clauses.rationale: IA-05 changes or refreshes authenticators on a schedule the organisation sets. IA-05(01) screens each new password against a list of commonly used, expected or compromised passwords, and enforces the composition rules the organisation chooses.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a password history that rejects any of the user's last four passwords. Add that check to the rules set under IA-05(01).

clauses.title: Authentication guidance and rules given to every user
clauses.rationale: IA-01 documents the authentication policy and procedures and shares them with the roles the organisation names. IA-05 requires individuals to take specific steps to protect their authenticators. PL-04 gives users written rules on their responsibilities and collects their acknowledgement. IR-06 has staff report suspected incidents, such as a compromised password, within a set time.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the guidance to tell users to avoid reusing old passwords and to change a password at once if they suspect a compromise. Add both points to the PL-04 rules.

clauses.title: Password-only logons: 90-day change or risk-based access
clauses.rationale: IA-05 changes or refreshes authenticators at intervals the organisation sets for each type, or when set events occur. IA-10 asks for extra authentication in situations the organisation defines, which supports deciding access from account risk.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for passwords used as the only factor to change at least every 90 days. The organisation may instead decide access by account risk in real time. Set the period in IA-05.

clauses.title: Customer password-only logons at service providers
clauses.rationale: IA-08 identifies and authenticates people outside the organisation, such as the service provider's customers. IA-05 changes or refreshes authenticators at intervals the organisation sets. IA-10 asks for extra authentication in situations the organisation defines, which supports deciding access from account risk.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the service provider to change customer passwords used alone at least every 90 days. It may instead judge each customer's access by account risk in real time. Set the period in IA-05.

clauses.title: One user per token, smart card or certificate
clauses.rationale: IA-02 uniquely identifies and authenticates each user, so each authentication binds to one person. IA-05 has individuals protect the authenticators issued to them. IA-05(02) enforces authorised access to each private key and maps the authenticated identity to the holder's account.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for each token, smart card or certificate to be issued to one person. Protect each one with a PIN or similar, so only its holder can use it.

clauses.title: Multi-factor authentication for admin access into the CDE
clauses.rationale: IA-02 uniquely identifies and authenticates each of the organisation's users. IA-02(01) asks for multi-factor authentication on privileged accounts, which covers administrators who reach the CDE over a network.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Multi-factor authentication for every user entering the CDE
clauses.rationale: IA-02 uniquely identifies and authenticates each of the organisation's users. IA-02(01) and (02) ask for multi-factor authentication on privileged and non-privileged accounts. Every user who reaches the CDE over a network then needs two or more factors.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 sets multi-factor authentication by type of account. PCI DSS sets it by path into the CDE. Ask for it again at the CDE boundary, even from users who used it to join the network remotely.

clauses.title: Multi-factor authentication for remote access from outside
clauses.rationale: AC-17 sets the conditions for each type of remote access and authorises it before connections start. IA-02(01) and (02) ask for multi-factor authentication on privileged and non-privileged accounts, and IA-02(06) puts one factor on a separate device. NIST writes IA-02 for the organisation's own users. IA-08 authenticates people from outside, such as vendors and customers.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Multi-factor authentication that resists replay and bypass
clauses.rationale: IA-02(08) asks for replay-resistant authentication on the privileged and non-privileged accounts the organisation selects. IA-02(01) and (02) ask for multi-factor authentication on both kinds of account, which combines factors of different types.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS lets users, administrators included, bypass multi-factor authentication only under a documented, time-limited exception that management approves. Grant access only once every factor has succeeded.

clauses.title: Interactive use of system accounts by approved exception
clauses.rationale: AC-02 defines and documents the types of account allowed on each system. AC-02(11) enforces the usage conditions the organisation sets for system accounts, such as interactive use only in approved cases. IA-02(05) authenticates each person before granting access to a shared account, so each action traces to one person.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS allows interactive use of application and system accounts only as a documented, time-limited exception that management approves. Record the business reason and the approval each time.

clauses.title: Keeping system account passwords out of code and scripts
clauses.rationale: IA-05 protects authenticator content from disclosure and change. IA-05(07) keeps unencrypted static authenticators out of applications and other static storage, such as scripts and configuration files. That covers the passwords of application and system accounts.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for these passwords to stay out of scripts, code and configuration files, in encrypted form too. Keep them in a secrets vault that applications call at run time.

clauses.title: Change schedule and strength for system account passwords
clauses.rationale: IA-05 changes or refreshes authenticators at intervals the organisation sets and after set events, such as a suspected compromise. IA-05(01) enforces the organisation's composition and complexity rules for passwords. RA-03 provides the risk assessment from which the organisation sets how often each password changes.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the complexity of each application or system account password to suit how often it changes. Set the IA-05(01) rules for each account to match its change interval.

clauses.title: Policies and procedures for physical security
clauses.rationale: PE-01 and MP-01 ask for documented policies and procedures for physical protection and for media protection. Each is shared with the people who need it and reviewed on a set cycle. Together they govern how the organisation controls entry to its sites and handles media with cardholder data.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the procedures to be in daily use and known to all who apply them. Check that staff follow them.

clauses.title: Roles and duties for physical security
clauses.rationale: PE-01 and MP-01 set out roles and responsibilities in the physical protection and media protection policies. PS-09 writes those security duties into position descriptions, so each one belongs to a named job. AT-03 gives role-based training to the people who hold them, and AT-03(02) trains them to use and run the physical security controls.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the people given these duties to understand them. Confirm that each one does, for example with a briefing or a signed acknowledgement.

clauses.title: Controlled entry to facilities that house CDE systems
clauses.rationale: PE-02 keeps the approved list of people allowed into the facility and issues the credentials they use. PE-03 verifies each person's authorisation at the facility's entry and exit points, using badge readers, locks or guards. PE-03(01) enforces the same authorisations again at the spaces that hold CDE systems.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Camera or badge records of who enters sensitive areas
clauses.rationale: PE-03 keeps physical access audit logs at the entry and exit points the organisation chooses. PE-06 monitors physical access and reviews the logs. PE-06(03) adds video surveillance, with recordings reviewed and kept for a period the organisation sets. PE-06(04) extends the monitoring to the rooms that hold the systems themselves.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for cameras and badge readers to be guarded against tampering and switching off. Compare their records with other entry data. Keep the records at least three months where the law allows, and set that period in PE-06(03).

clauses.title: Controlling network jacks in public areas
clauses.rationale: PE-04 controls physical access to network cabling and outlets inside the facility, for example by disconnecting or locking spare jacks. IA-03 identifies and authenticates each device, for instance through 802.1X, before it connects. Only known devices can then use a public jack.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Physical security of network hardware and telecom lines
clauses.rationale: PE-03 enforces physical access at the entry points the organisation chooses, inner doors included. PE-03(04) puts exposed devices, such as wireless access points, in lockable casings. PE-04 controls physical access to cabling and telecom lines inside the facility. PE-18 positions components where unauthorised people have the least chance to reach them.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Locking unattended consoles inside sensitive areas
clauses.rationale: AC-11 locks a device after a period of inactivity the organisation sets, or when the user locks it before leaving. The lock holds until the user signs in again with the usual identification and authentication.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for every console in a sensitive area to lock whenever it's left idle. Apply the AC-11 lock to each of those consoles.

clauses.title: Staff badges and entry rights for the CDE
clauses.rationale: PE-02 approves and keeps the list of people allowed in, issues their credentials, reviews the list and removes people once their need ends. PS-05 reviews and adjusts physical access when someone changes role. PS-04 revokes credentials and recovers badges and keys when employment ends. PE-03 secures keys, combinations and other physical access devices.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the badge system itself to be protected. Let only named administrators use it or handle blank badge stock.

clauses.title: Role-based staff entry to sensitive areas
clauses.rationale: PE-02 authorises physical access, and PE-02(01) bases it on each person's position or role. PE-03(01) enforces those authorisations again at the spaces that hold system components. PE-03 also changes keys and combinations when holders leave. PS-04 revokes credentials and retrieves keys and cards when employment ends.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for access to be revoked the moment employment ends. Set the time period in PS-04 to immediate, and apply it to physical access too.

clauses.title: Approving and escorting visitors in the CDE
clauses.rationale: PE-02 authorises access for visitors as well as staff, and issues the badges they carry. PE-02(02) asks each visitor for two forms of identification.
