PE-03 verifies authorisation before entry, and escorts visitors and controls their activity in the circumstances the organisation defines.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for visitor badges that expire and look clearly different from staff badges. Issue one to every visitor.

clauses.title: Recovering visitor badges at departure or expiry
clauses.rationale: PE-02 removes people from the access list once their need for access ends, which closes a visitor's authorisation when the visit is over. PE-03 secures physical access devices and keeps an inventory of them, so the organisation can track each visitor badge it issues.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for each visitor badge to be handed back or switched off before the visitor leaves, or on its expiry date. Make that part of signing visitors out.

clauses.title: Visitor log for the building and sensitive areas
clauses.rationale: PE-08 keeps visitor access records for a period the organisation sets, reviews them and reports anomalies. Its guidance lists who visited, for which organisation, and the dates and times of access among the details to record.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the log to name the person who authorised each visit. Keep it three months or longer where the law allows, and set that period in PE-08.

clauses.title: Securing all media that holds cardholder data
clauses.rationale: MP-02 limits access to digital and paper media to the people or roles the organisation names. MP-04 physically controls media and stores it securely in controlled areas, such as a locked cabinet or media library, until it is destroyed or sanitised.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Secure storage for offline backup media
clauses.rationale: MP-04 stores backup media securely in controlled areas. CP-09 protects the confidentiality, integrity and availability of backup information. CP-09(03) keeps backups of critical software and security information in a separate facility or a fire-rated container. Where backups go off site, CP-06 asks the storage site to match the controls of the main site.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Annual security review of offline backup storage
clauses.rationale: CA-02 assesses the controls in a system and its operating environment at a frequency the organisation sets, and reports the results. Scoped to the offline backup location, that assessment gives the security review the requirement asks for.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the security of each offline backup location to be inspected at least every 12 months. Set that frequency in CA-02.

clauses.title: Classifying media by how sensitive its data is
clauses.rationale: RA-02 categorises a system's information by the impact its loss would have, and records the result. That category sets how sensitive the media holding the information is. MP-03 marks media with the information's handling caveats, distribution limits and any security markings.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a classification on every item of media that holds cardholder data. Apply it to paper as well as electronic media.

clauses.title: Tracked delivery of media sent off site
clauses.rationale: MP-05 protects media carried outside controlled areas and keeps accountability for it in transit. It documents each transport and limits the work to authorised people. MP-05(03) puts a named custodian in charge of the media while it travels.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for media to travel by secure courier or another method that tracks each shipment. Keep logs that show where each item is while it's off site.

clauses.title: Manager approval before media leaves the site
clauses.rationale: MP-05 limits the transport of media outside controlled areas to authorised people and documents each movement. PE-16 authorises and controls system components leaving the facility, which can include media with cardholder data, and keeps records of them.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for someone with management authority to approve every movement of media off site, including media handed to individuals. Build that approval into the MP-05 transport process.

clauses.title: Inventory of electronic media holding cardholder data
clauses.rationale: CM-08 keeps a system component inventory at the level of detail needed for tracking and accountability, which can include storage devices. Under MP-04, physical control of stored media includes keeping inventories and accounting for each item.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for an inventory log that lists every item of electronic media holding cardholder data. Extend the CM-08 inventory to cover each of those items.

clauses.title: Yearly count of the electronic media inventory
clauses.rationale: CM-08 keeps the component inventory accurate and complete, and reviews and updates it at a frequency the organisation sets. Under MP-04, keeping inventories of stored media is part of controlling it physically.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the electronic media inventory to be counted and reconciled at least every 12 months. Set that frequency in CM-08.

clauses.title: Destroying paper records that hold cardholder data
clauses.rationale: MP-04 keeps media in secure storage until it is destroyed, which covers paper waiting for destruction. MP-06 sanitises media before disposal so the information is beyond recovery, and for paper its methods include destruction. SI-12 manages and retains information in line with legal and operational needs. SI-12(03) sets the techniques for destroying it once retention ends.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for paper to be destroyed by cross-cut shredding, incineration or pulping. Name those methods as the techniques in SI-12(03).

clauses.title: Destroying or wiping retired electronic media
clauses.rationale: MP-06 sanitises electronic media before disposal, release or reuse, by erasing or destroying it, so the data is beyond recovery. It matches the strength of the method to the security category of the information. SI-12 manages and retains information in line with legal and operational needs. SI-12(03) sets the techniques for disposing of or erasing it once retention ends.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Tamper protection for card-reading POI devices
clauses.rationale: SR-09 runs a tamper protection programme that guards components against modification and substitution. SR-10 inspects the components the organisation chooses, at set intervals or at random, to detect tampering. CM-08 keeps an inventory of the devices, so the organisation can tell when one goes missing or is swapped. AT-03 gives role-based training to staff who work with POI devices, covering how to spot and report tampering.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Current register of POI devices and their locations
clauses.rationale: CM-08 keeps a system component inventory with the details the organisation needs for accountability. Its guidance lists model, serial number, manufacturer and physical location among those details. CM-08(01) updates the inventory whenever devices are installed or removed.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Checking POI devices for skimmers and swapped units
clauses.rationale: SR-09 runs a tamper protection programme that covers the substitution of components as well as their modification. SR-10 inspects components at set intervals or at random to detect tampering.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for each inspection to cover the outer surfaces of every device. Check them for skimming overlays each time.

clauses.title: Risk-based frequency and type of POI checks
clauses.rationale: SR-10 lets the organisation choose which components to inspect for tampering, and when. RA-03 identifies threats and judges how likely and how harmful they are. That assessment gives the basis for the inspection schedule and method.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a targeted risk analysis that sets both how often the devices are inspected and how. Write it to cover every element of Requirement 12.3.1.

clauses.title: Training POI staff to spot tampering and impostors
clauses.rationale: AT-02 provides awareness training, and AT-02(03) teaches staff to recognise and report social engineering, such as a stranger posing as a repair technician. AT-02(04) covers suspicious communications and unusual system behaviour. AT-03 gives role-based training to staff in POI environments. MA-05 keeps a list of authorised maintenance people and checks the authorisation of anyone working unescorted. IR-06 requires staff to report suspected incidents, signs of tampering included.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for staff to be trained to verify each device before it's installed, replaced or returned. Make that check part of the AT-03 training.

clauses.title: Policies and procedures for audit logging
clauses.rationale: AU-01 asks for a documented audit and accountability policy, with procedures that put it into practice. The organisation shares both with the people who need them and reviews them on a set cycle. They govern the audit controls, from logging events to reviewing and keeping the records.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the procedures to be in daily use and known to all who apply them. Include time synchronisation in them, and check that staff follow them.

clauses.title: Roles and duties for audit logging
clauses.rationale: AU-01 asks for an audit and accountability policy that sets out roles and responsibilities, and for an official who manages it. PS-09 writes the logging and log review duties into position descriptions. AT-03 gives role-based training to the people in those roles, before they start and at set intervals afterwards.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the people given these duties to understand them. Confirm that each one does, for example with a briefing or a signed acknowledgement.

clauses.title: Audit logging on every in-scope system and cardholder data store
clauses.rationale: AU-02 has the organisation choose the event types each system logs, and explain why they will support later investigations. AU-12 makes the chosen system components generate audit records for those events.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for logging on every in-scope system component and wherever cardholder data is held. List all of them as the components AU-12 covers.

clauses.title: Logging each user's access to cardholder data
clauses.rationale: AU-02 has the organisation select user access to cardholder data as an event type to log. AU-12 generates a record of each access, including the identity of the user.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Logging everything done with administrator rights
clauses.rationale: AC-06(09) logs each time someone runs a privileged function. AU-02 has the organisation select administrator actions as event types to log, and AU-12 generates those records on each component.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS also asks for a record of any interactive use of application and system accounts. Add it to the event types in AU-02.

clauses.title: Logging every access to the audit logs themselves
clauses.rationale: AU-02 has the organisation select access to the audit logs as an event type to log. AU-12 then generates a record of each such access, with the identity of whoever made it.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Logging failed logons and other invalid access attempts
clauses.rationale: AU-02 has the organisation select failed logons and other invalid access attempts as event types to log. AU-12 generates a record of each failed attempt on the components it covers.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Logging changes to accounts, credentials and privileges
clauses.rationale: AC-02(04) automatically audits the creation, modification, enabling, disabling and removal of accounts. AU-02 has the organisation select changes to accounts and credentials as event types to log, and AU-12 generates a record of each change.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Logging audit logs being created, started, stopped or paused
clauses.rationale: AU-02 has the organisation choose the event types it logs, which can include the start, stop and pause of audit logging. AU-12 generates those records on each component that logs.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks each component to record when its audit logging starts, stops or pauses, and when a new log begins. Check that every platform captures these events.

clauses.title: Logging added and removed system-level objects
clauses.rationale: AU-02 has the organisation select the adding and removal of system-level objects as event types to log. AU-12 generates a record of each such change.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Details recorded in each audit log entry
clauses.rationale: AU-03 asks each audit record to show the type of event, when and where it occurred, its source and its outcome. It also gives the identity of any person or object linked to the event.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Limiting who can read the audit logs
clauses.rationale: AC-06 grants each person only the access their job needs, log files included. AU-09 protects audit information from unauthorised access. AU-09(06) gives read-only access to a named subset of privileged users or roles. AU-09(04) lets only a chosen subset of them manage audit logging.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Guarding stored audit logs against any change
clauses.rationale: AU-09 protects audit information from unauthorised change and deletion. AU-09(01) writes audit trails to hardware-enforced write-once media, and AU-09(03) protects their integrity with cryptography. AU-09(06) gives a named subset of privileged users read-only access.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Prompt backup of logs to central, tamper-resistant storage
clauses.rationale: AU-04(01) transfers audit logs from the system that produces them to a different system or media, at a frequency the organisation sets. AU-09(02) stores audit records on a physically separate system, and AU-09(01) writes them to write-once media.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for logs to reach a central internal log server promptly, those from external-facing systems included. Set the transfer frequency in AU-04(01) to meet that.

clauses.title: Integrity monitoring that alerts on changes to logs
clauses.rationale: AU-09 alerts named staff when someone changes or deletes audit information without authority. SI-07 runs integrity verification tools over the information the organisation names, here the stored logs. SI-07(02) notifies named people of any discrepancy those tools find.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Daily log review for the CDE and security-critical systems
clauses.rationale: AU-06 reviews and analyses audit records for unusual activity, at a frequency the organisation sets, and reports what it finds. AU-06(04) lets reviewers analyse records from many components in one place.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a daily review of security events and of the logs from CDE systems, critical systems and systems with security functions. Set AU-06 to that frequency.

clauses.title: Automated tools for audit log review
clauses.rationale: AU-06(01) brings automated mechanisms into log review, analysis and reporting. AU-07 provides tools to reduce audit records and report on them, and AU-07(01) sorts and searches them by chosen fields. SI-04(02) uses automated tools for near real-time analysis of events.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Regular log review for the remaining in-scope systems
clauses.rationale: AU-06 reviews and analyses audit records for unusual activity at a frequency the organisation sets, and reports findings to named roles.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Review cycle for other logs, set by targeted risk analysis
clauses.rationale: AU-06 lets the organisation set how often it reviews audit records, and adjust the level of review when risk changes. RA-03 assesses and documents the risk to the system, which gives a basis for that frequency.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the review frequency to come from a targeted risk analysis that meets every element of Requirement 12.3.1. Document that analysis alongside the RA-03 results.

clauses.title: Following up anomalies found in log review
clauses.rationale: AU-06 reports the findings of each log review to named roles so they can act on them. IR-04 handles the anomalies that prove to be incidents, from analysis and containment to recovery.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for action on every exception and anomaly the review finds. Track each one to closure and record the outcome.

clauses.title: Keeping 12 months of logs, the latest three online
clauses.rationale: AU-11 retains audit records for a period the organisation sets, to support later investigations, and AU-11(01) keeps long-term records retrievable. AU-04 allocates enough log storage to hold records for that period.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS sets retention at 12 months or more, with the latest three months ready for immediate analysis. Set those periods in AU-11 and size AU-04 storage to match.

clauses.title: Clock synchronisation on every system
clauses.rationale: SC-45 synchronises clocks within and between systems and their components. AU-08 uses those internal clocks to time-stamp audit records, in UTC or with a stated offset from it.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Central time servers fed by trusted outside sources
clauses.rationale: SC-45(01) compares system clocks with an authoritative time source at a set frequency, and corrects any drift beyond a set limit. SC-45(02) names a secondary source in another region for use when the primary is unavailable. AU-08 records time stamps in UTC or with a stated offset from it.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for designated central time servers that peer with each other. Only they take outside time, from chosen sources based on UTC or International Atomic Time. Point every other system at them.

clauses.title: Restricting and logging changes to time settings
clauses.rationale: AC-06 limits access to time data to the people who need it. AC-06(01) reserves access to security functions and security-relevant information, such as the time configuration, for named roles. AU-02 has the organisation select changes to time settings as an event type to log. AU-12 generates those records, and AU-06 reviews them.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the organisation to monitor and review each change to time settings on its critical systems. Make those systems part of the AU-06 review.

clauses.title: Prompt alerts when a critical security control fails
clauses.rationale: AU-05 alerts named staff when audit logging fails and takes the actions the organisation sets. SI-06 checks that chosen security functions work, and alerts staff and acts when a check fails. CA-07 monitors how well controls work on an ongoing basis and responds to what it finds.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS lists the security systems to watch for failure, physical access and segmentation controls among them. Name each one among the functions SI-06 checks, and alert and act on failures promptly.

clauses.title: Recovery and follow-up after a security control fails
clauses.rationale: IR-04 handles each failure as an incident, from containment to recovery, and feeds lessons learned back into procedures. IR-05 tracks and documents each one. SI-02(07) finds the root cause of a failure, then puts fixes in place and checks that they work.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the organisation to look for security problems that came up while the control was down, and to confirm that monitoring has resumed. Add both steps to the incident procedures.

clauses.title: Policies and procedures for security testing
clauses.rationale: CA-01, RA-01 and SI-01 ask for documented policies and procedures, shared with the people who need them and reviewed on a set cycle. CA-01's assessment policy governs penetration testing. RA-01's risk assessment policy governs vulnerability scanning. SI-01's integrity policy governs intrusion detection, change detection and payment page monitoring.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the procedures to be in daily use and known to all who apply them. Check that staff follow them in practice.

clauses.title: Roles and duties for security testing
clauses.rationale: CA-01, RA-01 and SI-01 each ask for a policy that sets out roles and responsibilities, here for the testing and monitoring work. PS-09 writes those duties into position descriptions. AT-03 trains people for their role before they take on its duties, and again at a frequency the organisation sets.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the people given these duties to understand them. Confirm that each one does, for example with a briefing or a signed acknowledgement.

clauses.title: Quarterly checks for rogue wireless access points
clauses.rationale: CM-08(03) uses automated tools to detect unauthorised hardware, such as a wireless access point, at a frequency the organisation sets. It then acts on each one it finds. SI-04(14) runs wireless intrusion detection to identify rogue wireless devices. SI-04(05) alerts named staff when the system generates signs of compromise.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a search for wireless access points at least once every three months. Set that frequency in CM-08(03).

clauses.title: Wireless access point inventory with business reasons
clauses.rationale: CM-08 keeps an accurate inventory of system components, and here it lists each approved wireless access point. AC-18 sets the requirements for each type of wireless access and authorises it before connections are allowed. That approval is the basis for each access point on the list.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a written business reason for each approved access point. CM-08 lets the organisation choose what the inventory records, so add the reason there.

clauses.title: Quarterly internal vulnerability scans and rescans
clauses.rationale: RA-05 scans for vulnerabilities at a frequency the organisation sets and remediates them by risk. RA-05(02) updates the vulnerabilities the tool checks for. CA-02 selects a suitable assessor, CA-02(01) makes the assessor independent and CA-02(02) adds vulnerability scanning to control assessments. SI-02 corrects the flaws the scans find.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for internal scans at least once every three months. Set that frequency in RA-05, and rescan to confirm each high-risk and critical finding is fixed.

clauses.title: Risk-based fixing of lower-ranked vulnerabilities
clauses.rationale: RA-03 assesses risk by identifying threats and vulnerabilities and judging the likelihood and size of harm. It documents the results. RA-05 remediates vulnerabilities within response times the organisation sets from its assessment of risk. SI-02 identifies, reports and corrects system flaws, the lower-ranked ones included.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the timing of these fixes to come from a targeted risk analysis that meets requirement 12.3.1. Use that analysis to set the RA-05 response times.

clauses.title: Authenticated internal vulnerability scanning
clauses.rationale: RA-05(05) authorises privileged access for scanning on the components the organisation names, which lets scans run with credentials. RA-05(03) sets how broad and deep the scanning goes. AC-02 manages each scanning account like any other account, those that allow interactive logon included.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a record of every system that rejects scan credentials. Keep that list current and store it with the scan results.

clauses.title: Internal scanning after each significant change
clauses.rationale: CM-04 analyses each change for its security impact before it goes in, and CM-04(02) checks the affected controls once it is made. RA-05 scans when new vulnerabilities may affect the system and remediates them by risk. CA-02 selects the assessor, and CA-02(01) makes the assessor independent. SI-02 corrects the high-risk and critical flaws the scan finds.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for an internal scan after every significant change. Build that scan into the change process so each significant change triggers one.

clauses.title: Quarterly external scans by an Approved Scanning Vendor
clauses.rationale: CA-02 selects the right assessor for each type of assessment, here an outside scanning vendor, and CA-02(01) makes that assessor independent. RA-05 scans for vulnerabilities at a frequency the organisation sets and remediates them by risk. SI-02 corrects the flaws the external scans report.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for an external scan every three months by an Approved Scanning Vendor. Each quarter's scan must meet the ASV Program Guide's criteria for a pass, so rescan until it does.

clauses.title: External scanning after each significant change
clauses.rationale: CM-04 analyses each change for its security impact, and CM-04(02) verifies the affected controls after the change. RA-05 scans for vulnerabilities, here from outside the network, and remediates them by risk. CA-02 selects the assessor, and CA-02(01) makes the assessor independent. SI-02 corrects the flaws the scan finds.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for every finding with a CVSS score of 4.0 or higher to be fixed. Set that threshold in RA-05 and rescan to confirm each fix.

clauses.title: Penetration testing methodology and what it covers
clauses.rationale: CA-02 asks for an assessment plan that sets the scope and procedures of each assessment and is approved before it starts. Here that plan serves as the penetration testing methodology. CA-08 runs penetration tests on the systems the organisation names, at a frequency it sets.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS sets out what the methodology must include. Cover segmentation testing, the application and network layers and the threats seen in the past year. Keep test results and remediation records for at least 12 months.

clauses.title: Internal penetration tests, yearly and after major changes
clauses.rationale: CA-08 runs penetration tests on the systems the organisation names, at a frequency it sets, here from inside the network. CA-08(01) gives the testing to an independent agent or team.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for an internal test at least once a year and again after any significant upgrade or change. Put both in the CA-08 test schedule.

clauses.title: External penetration tests, yearly and after major changes
clauses.rationale: CA-08 runs penetration tests on the systems the organisation names, at a frequency it sets, here from outside the network. CA-08(01) hands the testing to an independent agent or team.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for an external test at least once a year and again after any significant upgrade or change. Put both in the CA-08 test schedule.

clauses.title: Fixing and retesting penetration test findings
clauses.rationale: CA-05 records the planned fix for each weakness the tests find and keeps that plan up to date. RA-07 responds to each finding in line with the organisation's risk tolerance. SI-02 corrects the flaws. CA-08 runs the penetration tests, here repeated to confirm each fix works.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Yearly penetration tests of CDE segmentation
clauses.rationale: CA-02 assesses whether controls work as intended, here whether segmentation keeps the CDE apart from other networks. CA-08 runs penetration tests on the segmentation controls at a frequency the organisation sets, and CA-08(01) gives the work to an independent tester or team.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a test of every segmentation method once a year or more often, and after any change to it. Set that frequency in CA-08.

clauses.title: Six-monthly segmentation tests for service providers
clauses.rationale: CA-02 assesses whether controls work as intended, here whether segmentation isolates the CDE from systems out of scope. CA-08 runs penetration tests on the segmentation controls at a frequency the organisation sets. CA-08(01) gives the tests to an independent tester or team.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the service provider to test every segmentation method every six months or more often, and after any change to it. Set that frequency in CA-08.

clauses.title: Multi-tenant providers' support for customer penetration tests
clauses.rationale: CA-08 runs penetration tests on the systems the organisation names, here the infrastructure each customer subscribes to. CA-02 gives the results of each assessment to the people or roles the organisation names, here its customers.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the multi-tenant service provider to support each customer's external penetration testing. Give each customer evidence of external tests on its infrastructure that meet requirement 11.4.3, or prompt access to run its own.

clauses.title: Intrusion detection and prevention for CDE traffic
clauses.rationale: SC-07 monitors and controls traffic at the external boundary and at key internal interfaces. SI-04 monitors the system for attacks and signs of attack. SI-04(01) ties the intrusion detection tools together across the whole system, SI-04(04) watches inbound and outbound traffic, and SI-04(05) alerts staff to signs of compromise.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for current signatures, baselines and detection engines on every intrusion detection and prevention tool. Update them as part of SI-04 monitoring.

clauses.title: Service providers' detection of covert malware channels
clauses.rationale: SC-07(09) detects and denies outgoing traffic that threatens external systems, and SC-07(10) prevents exfiltration. SI-04(18) analyses outbound traffic at the boundary and at chosen interior points to find covert exfiltration. SI-04(11) analyses the same traffic for anomalies.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the service provider to detect and deal with covert command-and-control channels, such as DNS tunnelling. Point the sensors at those routes and respond to every alert.

clauses.title: Weekly integrity checks on critical files
clauses.rationale: SI-07 uses integrity verification tools to detect unauthorised changes to the software, firmware and information the organisation names, here its critical files. SI-07(01) runs integrity checks at a frequency the organisation sets. SI-07(02) notifies named staff when a check finds a discrepancy.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for critical files to be compared at least once a week. Set that frequency in SI-07(01).

clauses.title: Detecting tampering with payment page scripts and headers
clauses.rationale: SC-18 sets which mobile code, such as JavaScript, is acceptable, and monitors and controls its use, here on payment pages. SI-07 detects unauthorised changes to named information, here the page scripts and headers, and SI-07(02) notifies staff when it finds one. SI-04 watches for signs of attack, and SI-04(24) gathers known indicators of compromise.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the check to see headers and scripts as the shopper's browser receives them. Run it at least once a week, or on a schedule set by a targeted risk analysis under requirement 12.3.1.

clauses.title: Information security policy shared with staff and partners
clauses.rationale: PM-01 asks for an organisation-wide information security programme plan that sets out the programme's requirements and the controls that meet them. A senior official approves it. The organisation shares it and keeps it up to date on a cycle it sets.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for the policy to reach relevant vendors and business partners as well as staff. Send each of them the current version.

clauses.title: Yearly review and update of the security policy
clauses.rationale: PM-01 has the organisation review and update its information security programme plan at a frequency it sets. The organisation also updates the plan after events it defines, such as a change in business objectives or risk.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS sets a review at least every 12 months. Set that frequency in PM-01.

clauses.title: Security duties for all staff and their acknowledgement
clauses.rationale: PM-01's programme plan identifies security roles and responsibilities and assigns them. PS-09 writes security duties into each position description. PL-04 gives each person who needs access the rules for their security responsibilities, and receives their documented acknowledgement before granting it.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: An executive in charge of information security
clauses.rationale: PM-02 appoints a senior information security officer, such as a CISO, to lead the organisation-wide security programme. It gives that officer the mission and the resources to develop the programme and keep it running.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Acceptable use rules for end-user technology
clauses.rationale: PL-04 sets rules of behaviour for using information and systems, and collects each user's documented acknowledgement. AC-19 sets configuration and connection requirements for mobile devices and authorises each connection. CM-07(05) and (09) keep lists of the software and hardware approved for use and block everything else.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for acceptable use rules for each end-user technology, such as laptops, phones, removable media, email and internet use. Record who approved each technology for use.

clauses.title: Targeted risk analysis for frequencies the organisation sets
clauses.rationale: RA-03 has the organisation identify threats and vulnerabilities and judge the likelihood and impact of harm. The organisation documents the results and reviews them at a frequency it sets. It updates the assessment after significant changes.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a separate written analysis for each requirement that lets the organisation choose a frequency. Justify each chosen frequency, and review each analysis at least every 12 months.

clauses.title: Targeted risk analysis for the customised approach
clauses.rationale: RA-03 provides the documented risk analysis behind each customised control. PL-02's security plan describes the controls in place and the reasons for any tailoring, and can serve as the controls matrix. The authorising official approves the plan before it takes effect.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS Appendix D lists the evidence each customised control needs, such as a controls matrix. Prepare it, and repeat the analysis at least every 12 months.

clauses.title: Inventory and yearly review of cipher suites and protocols
clauses.rationale: SC-13 has the organisation determine each use of cryptography and the type of cryptography that use requires. SI-05 receives security alerts and advisories from outside organisations on an ongoing basis, such as news that an algorithm or protocol has weakened.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a list of every cipher suite and protocol in use, with its purpose and location. Review it at least every 12 months, and keep a plan for replacing any that weaken.

clauses.title: Yearly review of vendor support for technology in use
clauses.rationale: SA-22 replaces components once their supplier stops supporting them, or arranges other support for them. CA-05 records planned remediation in a plan of action and milestones, here the replacement of outdated technology.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a review of all hardware and software at least every 12 months, recording any vendor end-of-life notices. Have senior management approve the plan to replace outdated technology.

clauses.title: Executive accountability for PCI DSS compliance
clauses.rationale: PM-01 has a senior official, accountable for the risk, approve the organisation-wide security programme plan. The plan assigns roles and responsibilities and covers compliance. PM-02 appoints a senior information security officer to lead the programme, with the mission and resources it needs.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks executive management to hold overall accountability for PCI DSS compliance. Write a charter for the compliance programme and report on it to executive management.

clauses.title: Quarterly checks that staff follow security procedures
clauses.rationale: CA-02 assesses whether controls operate as intended, at a frequency the organisation sets, and CA-02(01) uses independent assessors. CA-07 runs ongoing control assessments, and CA-07(01) has independent assessors do the monitoring. CA-07(05) checks that policies are in place and that controls run consistently.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS sets these checks at least every three months. Set that frequency in CA-02 and CA-07, and cover each task the requirement lists, such as log reviews and change control.

clauses.title: Recording the quarterly checks and their sign-off
clauses.rationale: CA-02 produces a report of each assessment and gives the results to the roles the organisation names. CA-05 documents the planned remediation of each weakness found, in a plan of action and milestones.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the owner of the compliance programme to review and sign off the results. Name that owner among the roles that receive the CA-02 report.

clauses.title: Inventory of in-scope system components
clauses.rationale: CM-08 keeps an accurate, complete inventory of system components, with the details the organisation sets for accountability. The organisation reviews and updates it at a frequency it chooses.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for each component's function or use in the inventory. Add it to the details CM-08 records.

clauses.title: Confirming PCI DSS scope every year
clauses.rationale: CM-08 inventories every component in the system. CM-12 records where account data is processed and stored, on which components, and each change of location. CA-03 approves each exchange of information with other systems, including those of third parties, and documents it in an agreement. PL-02's security plan defines the system's components, operating environment and connections. The organisation reviews the plan on a cycle it sets.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS sets a scope check at least every 12 months and after each significant change. Set that cycle for the PL-02 review. Cover the data flows, and justify each network that segmentation keeps out of scope.

clauses.title: Confirming PCI DSS scope every six months
clauses.rationale: CM-08 inventories every component in the system. CM-12 records where account data is processed and stored, and on which components. CA-03 documents each exchange of information with other systems, third parties included, in an agreement. PL-02's security plan defines the system's components and connections, and the organisation reviews it on a cycle it sets.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the service provider to confirm its scope at least every six months and after each significant change. Set that cycle for the PL-02 review.

clauses.title: Scope and control review after a reorganisation
clauses.rationale: PL-02 updates the security plan when the system or its operating environment changes. RA-03 updates the risk assessment after significant changes and shares the results with the roles the organisation names.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS treats a significant change in the organisation's structure as a trigger for a written review of scope and controls. Report the results to executive management.

clauses.title: Formal security awareness programme for all staff
clauses.rationale: AT-01 asks for a documented awareness and training policy and procedures, shared with the people who need them and reviewed on a set cycle. AT-02 gives security awareness training to every user of the system, managers and contractors included. Together they make awareness a formal programme.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Yearly review and refresh of awareness content
clauses.rationale: AT-02 updates awareness content at a frequency the organisation sets and after events it names. It also builds lessons from security incidents, inside and outside the organisation, into the training.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS sets a review of the awareness programme at least once every 12 months. Set that frequency in AT-02.

clauses.title: Awareness training at hire and yearly, with policy sign-off
clauses.rationale: AT-02 trains new users when they start and again at a frequency the organisation sets, using awareness techniques it chooses. PL-04 gets each user's documented acknowledgement of the rules of behaviour, and asks for it again at a set frequency or when the rules change.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Teaching staff to spot phishing and social engineering
clauses.rationale: AT-02 gives security awareness training to all users. AT-02(03) trains them to recognise and report social engineering, and AT-02(04) to recognise suspicious communications such as phishing emails. AT-02(01) adds practical exercises that simulate incidents, such as a staged phishing attack.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Acceptable use rules in awareness training
clauses.rationale: PL-04 sets the rules for each user's responsibilities and expected behaviour in using information and systems, which covers acceptable use. AT-02 provides awareness training that can carry those rules. SP 800-53 accepts training that covers the rules as the acknowledgement PL-04 asks for.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Background checks before hiring staff with CDE access
clauses.rationale: PS-02 gives every position a risk designation and sets screening criteria for the people who fill it. PS-03 screens each person before they are given access to the system, and screens them again under conditions the organisation sets.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Inventory of service providers that touch account data
clauses.rationale: PM-30 sets an organisation-wide strategy for supply chain risk, and PM-30(01) identifies, prioritises and assesses the suppliers of critical products and services. SA-09 defines and documents the oversight, roles and responsibilities for each external service the organisation uses.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a list of every service provider that holds account data or could affect its security. Describe what each one provides, and keep the list current.

clauses.title: Contracts where service providers accept responsibility for data
clauses.rationale: SA-04 writes security requirements into each contract and names the parties responsible for information security. SA-09 requires providers of external services to meet the organisation's security requirements, and documents the oversight, roles and responsibilities that go with each service.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks each service provider to accept, in writing, responsibility for the account data it handles or could affect. Get that acknowledgement into every service provider agreement.

clauses.title: Due diligence before taking on a service provider
clauses.rationale: SR-06 assesses and reviews the supply chain risks of each supplier and the services it provides. SR-05 sets the acquisition strategies and procurement methods that guard against supply chain risk, and SR-05(02) assesses a service before it is selected. SA-09(01) assesses risk and gets approval before the organisation outsources information security services.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a set process for engaging service providers, with due diligence done before the agreement is signed. Write that process down and apply it to every new provider.

clauses.title: Yearly check of each service provider's PCI DSS status
clauses.rationale: SA-09 monitors each external provider's compliance with the required controls on an ongoing basis, by methods the organisation chooses. SR-06 reviews the risks of each supplier and its services at a frequency the organisation sets.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the organisation to check, at least once every 12 months, each service provider's compliance status. Set that frequency in SR-06.

clauses.title: Responsibility split for PCI DSS requirements, per provider
clauses.rationale: SA-04 allocates responsibility for information security between the parties in each contract. SA-09 defines and documents the organisation's oversight and the roles and responsibilities that go with each external service.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a record of which PCI DSS requirements each service provider manages, which the organisation manages and which they share. Keep it as a responsibility matrix for each provider.

clauses.title: Service provider's written acknowledgement to customers
clauses.rationale: CA-03 records each party's security requirements, controls and responsibilities in the agreement that governs an exchange of information. SA-09 is the customer's side of the same duty: it requires providers of external services to meet the customer's security requirements.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the service provider to accept, in writing, responsibility for the account data it handles for each customer or could affect. Put that acknowledgement in every customer agreement.

clauses.title: Service provider's answers to customer compliance requests
clauses.rationale: SA-09 is the customer's side of this duty: it monitors each provider's control compliance and documents the roles and responsibilities around each service. SR-08 sets agreements with the parties in a supply chain to share the results of assessments and audits, such as a PCI DSS compliance status.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the service provider to give customers, when they ask, its PCI DSS compliance status and the split of responsibilities for each service. Set up a way to answer those requests.

clauses.title: Incident response plan and what it covers
clauses.rationale: IR-08 sets out the incident response plan, with its structure, the incidents to report, how incident information is shared and who is responsible. IR-04 handles incidents through containment, eradication and recovery, in step with contingency planning. IR-06 reports incident information to the authorities the organisation names. CP-02 covers business recovery and continuity, and CP-09 provides the backups the plan relies on.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the plan to name the payment brands and acquirers to notify and to include the brands' own response procedures. Add an analysis of the legal duties to report a compromise.

clauses.title: Yearly incident response plan review and full test
clauses.rationale: IR-08 has the plan reviewed and approved at a frequency the organisation sets, and updated after changes or problems found in use or testing. IR-03 tests how well the incident response capability works, at a set frequency and with tests the organisation chooses.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a review and a full test of the plan at least once every 12 months, covering each element of 12.10.1. Set that frequency in IR-03 and IR-08.

clauses.title: Named incident responders on call around the clock
clauses.rationale: IR-08 designates the people or roles responsible for incident response. IR-04 handles incidents, and IR-04(14) adds a security operations centre that monitors systems and responds to incidents on an ongoing basis.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for named people available to respond at any hour of any day. Keep a 24/7 rota of named responders.

clauses.title: Training incident responders in their duties
clauses.rationale: IR-02 trains each person with an incident response role within a set time of taking it on, and again at a frequency the organisation sets. It also reviews and updates the training content on a set cycle and after events the organisation names.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Responder training frequency set by targeted risk analysis
clauses.rationale: IR-02 trains incident responders at a frequency the organisation sets. RA-03 supplies a documented risk assessment, weighing threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood and harm, on which the organisation can base that frequency.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a targeted risk analysis that sets the training frequency and covers every element of Requirement 12.3.1. Write that analysis and record the frequency it sets in IR-02.

clauses.title: Alert handling in the incident response plan
clauses.rationale: SI-04 monitors systems for attacks and unauthorised connections. SI-04(05) alerts named staff to signs of compromise, and SI-04(07) notifies incident responders and acts on suspicious events. SI-07(07) feeds the unauthorised changes it detects into incident response. IR-04 handles incidents from detection and analysis onward, and IR-08 sets out the plan and defines which incidents to report.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS names the alert sources the plan must cover. They include intrusion detection, network security controls, file change detection, payment page tamper alerts and wireless scans. Name each in the plan.

clauses.title: Updating the response plan from lessons and industry change
clauses.rationale: IR-04 builds lessons learned from incident handling into response procedures, training and testing. IR-08 updates the plan for changes to the system and the organisation, and for problems found while using or testing it.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS also asks for the plan to keep pace with industry developments. Add them to the events that trigger an update.

clauses.title: Responding when stored PAN turns up somewhere unexpected
clauses.rationale: IR-09 responds to information spills. It names who responds, identifies the data, isolates and cleans the affected system and looks for other systems the spill reached. IR-04 analyses the incident, contains it, recovers from it and turns lessons learned into changes.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the organisation to check whether sensitive authentication data sits alongside the stray PAN, and to trace how the data got there. Add both steps to the procedure.

clauses.title: Two-way separation of provider and customer environments
clauses.rationale: AC-03 enforces approved authorisations for logical access, so the provider and its customers reach each other's environments only when authorised. SC-07 controls traffic at the managed interfaces between them, and SC-07(21) uses boundary protection to isolate the components the organisation names. SC-50 enforces separation in software between security domains.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for separation in both directions. Check that customers reach the provider's environment, and the provider reaches theirs, only with authorisation.

clauses.title: Customer-to-customer separation of data and CDE
clauses.rationale: AC-03 enforces approved authorisations, so each customer's access stops at its own environment and data. SC-04 stops information passing between customers through shared resources, such as memory or storage that one user releases and the next reuses.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 states this more generally than PCI DSS. Check the controls against the requirement's own text.

clauses.title: Keeping each customer within its allocated resources
clauses.rationale: AC-03 enforces approved authorisations to system resources for each customer. SC-06 allocates resources such as processing, storage and bandwidth by quota or priority, so each customer stays within its share and the others keep theirs.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the service provider to hold each customer to its own allocation. Set quotas on each customer's compute, storage and network, and enforce them.

clauses.title: Penetration tests of customer separation every six months
clauses.rationale: CA-08 runs penetration tests on the systems the organisation names, at a frequency it sets. CA-02 assesses whether controls, here the separation between customer environments, work as intended and produce the desired outcome.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS sets penetration testing of the separation at least once every six months. Set that frequency in CA-08.

clauses.title: Audit logs for each customer, readable by that customer
clauses.rationale: AU-02 selects the events to log in each customer environment, and AU-12 generates audit records for them on the components the organisation names. AU-09 protects the logs from unauthorised access, so only the owning customer reads them. AU-16 coordinates audit information that crosses organisational boundaries, and AU-16(02) shares it with each customer under an agreement.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the service provider to tell each customer where its logs are. Keep their content and retention in line with Requirement 10.

clauses.title: Forensic investigation support for every customer
clauses.rationale: IR-07 offers a support resource for handling and reporting incidents, which can include access to forensic services. IR-04 handles incidents. IR-04(12) analyses malicious code and other traces an incident leaves behind, and IR-04(10) coordinates incident handling with the other organisations in the supply chain.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for prompt forensic support for any customer after a suspected or confirmed incident. Agree with each customer in advance how its investigators reach the evidence.

clauses.title: Customer reporting channel for incidents and vulnerabilities
clauses.rationale: IR-07 gives the system's users, customers included, a support resource for reporting incidents, and IR-04 handles the incidents they report. RA-05(11) sets up a public channel for vulnerability reports, and RA-05 remediates vulnerabilities in line with an assessment of risk. SI-02 identifies and corrects flaws in the system.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks for a secure channel for customer reports. Protect that channel, and tell customers about the issues that affect them.

clauses.title: Known-exploit check for POI terminals on SSL or early TLS
clauses.rationale: RA-05 monitors and scans for vulnerabilities at a frequency the organisation sets, and again when new ones are reported. Applied to the terminals, it shows whether any known SSL or early TLS exploit affects them.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the organisation to confirm that each terminal resists the known SSL and early TLS exploits. Keep evidence of this, such as vendor statements.

clauses.title: Service provider's plan to retire SSL and early TLS
clauses.rationale: RA-03 assesses the risk of the remaining SSL and early TLS connections and documents the results. RA-05 monitors for new vulnerabilities in those protocols. CM-03 reviews each proposed change for its security impact, which keeps the old protocols out of new environments. CA-05 sets out the migration as planned remediation, with milestones.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the plan to describe how SSL and early TLS are used. Record in it where they run and what data they carry.

clauses.title: Secure connection option for customers' POI terminals
clauses.rationale: SC-08 protects the confidentiality and integrity of data in transit, and SC-08(01) does it with cryptography. SC-13 has the organisation decide the type of cryptography each use requires, such as a current version of TLS.
clauses.gaps: PCI DSS asks the service provider to give every customer a connection option on a secure protocol version. Customers can then move their terminals off SSL and early TLS.
